question.prompt: Four friends do yardwork for their neighbors over the weekend, earning \(\$15,\) \(\$20,\) \(\$25,\) and \(\$40\) respectively. They decide to split their earnings equally among themselves. In total how much will the friend who earned \(\$40\) give to the others?

solutions.explanation:
An equal split means each friend finishes with one fourth of the total earnings. Together they earned

\[
15+20+25+40=100\text{ dollars},
\]

so each person's share is \(100/4=25\) dollars.

The friend who earned \(40\) dollars keeps \(25\) and gives away \(40-25=\boxed{15}\) dollars, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). This also fills the other friends' shortfalls of \(10\), \(5\), and \(0\) dollars.
solutions.title: Find the equal share and subtract it from the largest earning
